comment.narrative: A Mutual Capacity Strengthening baseline survey was conducted in 2021, screening seven different capacities under the topic of influencing and awareness raising on SRHR for young people. These are: developing an influencing strategy; youth-led influencing; lobby and/or advocacy on policies and practices; public campaigning; digital campaigning; working with traditional media; and influencing social norms. The topics which emerged as the ones with the most indicated needs among partners engaged at regional and global level: developing an influencing strategy; lobby and/or advocacy on policies and practices; youth-led influencing; and digital campaigning. The topics where partners most often indicated an offer on capacity strengthening were influencing social norms and working with traditional media. (Organisations could express a need, an offer, or both a need and offer on the same topic.

In relation to SRHR influencing capacity, Oxfam Novib and RNW Media maintained their capacity in 2025. Both partners did not report increased capacity in relation to SRHR influencing topics during the year. Based on the criteria agreed on, this did not result in an actual for KI-6 in 2025 for either of the two partners.

In relation to SRHR influencing capacity, based on the criteria agreed on, one not women or youth led organization (Oxfam Novib) realized an actual for KI-6 in 2024. Oxfam Novib reported increased capacity on Developing an influencing strategy; Lobby and/or advocacy SRHR policies and practices; Public campaigning; and Digital campaigning in 2024, resulting in an actual in 2024. The actual for Oxfam Novib is not included again here (nor in IATI) for KI-6 in 2024, as Oxfam Novib was already counted as an actual in 2022 for KI-6. A second women led partner of the Regional Platform, which had a target for 2022, did not yet report an increased capacity related to SRHR influencing with diverse young people since joining the programme. Plannedactivities for capacity strengthening were either postponed to 2023 or did not yet result in actuals in 2022. All three women led organisation expressed an interest to (further) increase several capacities related to SRHR influencing with diverse young people over the course of the programme.(Source: CATool 2022)Among activities related to capacity strengthening on SRHR influencing with diverse young people reported on for 2022 are the following. Hands-on support on advocacy was provided in 2022 throughdifferent trainings on SRHR, an art retreat and panel discussions by Regional Platform partners partners. The discussions on topics related to SRHR and addressing the importance of these terms in the MENA region with activists and different organisationsshall be reflected in their advocacy work whether through art, research, social media campaign, or any other formats. RNW Media has adopted Hootsuite instead of the data lake intervention planned for 2022. A short session on social listening was providedto the participants at the Annual Learning Event.

Regional partners will be capacitated on digital campaigning. One of the regional partners will be capacitated on youth-led influencing as well., and will develop its network of researchers on SRHR and expand its outreach and connections within the targeted countries.This will include increased capacities in online learning and advocacy. The Regional Policy Dialogue Meetings will offer partners a robust platform for practicing advocacy, as so will collaborative advocacy campaigns like the Enough Campaign. The women led partner will also get training on media management. In addition, it will will receive a training on feminist influencing from another gender justice programme than Masarouna. Oxfam Regional Platform representatives are familiar with the digital media solutions that RNW Media has to offer and can take advantage of these solutions that equip them with strategic mindset for online presence, awareness raising and advocacy campaigning, as well as use data insights to inform decision making. Oxfam Novib facilitated the regional/global level strategy revision by Masarouna influencing colleagues in 2023. From end 2023 the strategy will be implemented, comprising 4 clusters: Feminist Influencing, Narratives, Tec companies and CSE (the latter will be mainly implemented in collaboration with the youth advocates). Influencing narratives on SRHR/inclusion of marginalized groups will be developed by partners through "learning by doing" with support of Oxfam Novib. Overall, it is expected that partners will be more focused and hence efficient in their influencing activities, thanks to the knowledge and experience with developing and revising their own strategy. (Partners to be engaged, next to the Oxfam Regional Platform, still need to be identified; hence have not been included as a quantitative target for KI-6. )

In 2025, Oxfam Regional Platform (RP), in coordination with Oxfam Novib, will hold regular coordination meetings with consortium members,, Masarouna partners and Oxfam offices to strengthen the coordination of advocacy efforts among CSOs and youth. (Above-mentioned organisations are not included in the quantitative target for 2025, to avoid double counting with previous years)

comment.narrative:
In 2021, 6 organizations are involved in the programme at regional/global level (4 regional, 2 global). In 2022, 9 organisations (7 regional; 2 global): 1 regional partner is not involved anymore, and 4 new regional CSOs are engaged.
Building on our combined experience in the region, the consortium - in 2021 comprising of AFE, RNW Media and Oxfam Novib; and in 2022 of SMEX, Fe-Male, RNW Media and Oxfam Novib, joined by a regional strategic partner - is uniquely positioned to advance the fulfilment of SRHR for our target group of diverse young people. The consortium was built on common views and values. The partners’ experience, existing networks and long-term relationships in MENA legitimize the consortium’s ability to challenge social norms, stimulate discussion and strengthen civil society for increased government accountability. The consortium presents a cohesive and comprehensive response to SRHR programming needs in MENA. In 2022, 4 both women and youth led CSOs are engaged: regional consortium partners Fe-Male and SMEX, a regional strategic partner, and a 7th regional partner. Fe-Male as a regional feminist collective working in MENA strengthens the feminist focus of Masarouna and works with women and girls to eliminate injustice through building a young feminist movement and campaigning together against discriminatory norms and policies. SMEX has extensive experience and expertise on advancing digital rights in the Arab region through research, campaigns and advocacy encouring users to engagecritically with digital technologies, media and networks. The regional strategic partner brings to Masarouna a wealth of expertise on the rights of marginalized groups in the region. The 7th regional partner collaborated in organizing feminist circles aimed at creating safe spaces for feminist conversations amongst activists, feeding into policy dialogues and communication briefs and providing homegrown feminist knowledge strengthening on-going feminist praxis in MENA

On regional and global level, consortium members strive for equal partnership. In 2023, the partnership entails Oxfam Novib, RNW Media, SMEX, FEMALE, the strategic partner and the Oxfam Regional Platform. Consortium members work closely together on different levels and working towards more co-creation and mutual learning collaborations. Increasingly, partners work on joint advocacy, mutual capacity strengthening and support to each other’s activities. The outcomes of the jointly conducted MTR will serve as input to further strengthen the cooperation.
Oxfam Regional Platform has sustained the formal partnership with 1 both women and youth led organization, which has trained young activists and shared SRHR information, as well as organised several regional events that aimed at facilitating access to key global spaces such as the CSW.
FEMALE gained support from RNW Media on digital media through multiple sessions, and received support from Oxfam Novib in multiple areas such as M&E, finance and management. Following feedback from SMEX, FEMALE has implemented a digital security policy to safeguard privacy and enhance online safety measures for our contributors and users.
FEMALE selected 2 subgrantees in 2023. The strategic partner collaborated with 4organisations in their advocacy lab in 2023. SMEX collaborated with 8 organizations for their training on digital security and for the assessment of their digital hygiene. These are all existing or new Masarouna partners operating at country level and reported under the respective countries.

On regional and global level, consortium members strive for equal partnership. In 2024, the partnership entails Oxfam Novib, SMEX, FEMALE, the Strategic Partner and the Oxfam Regional Platform. RNW Media is closely working together with all these partners on different levels through several working groups and is working towards more co-creation, mutual learning collaborations and gathering collective learnings built on five years of partnership. In 2024, FEMALE, SMEX and the Regional Partner remained active partners in Masarouna. SMEX continued mutual capacity strengthening with a focus on digital security and resilience, and conducted a study on content moderation and SRHR on social media platforms, contributing to Masarouna’s work at the intersection of digital rights and SRHR. FEMALE collaborated with Oxfam in country on advocacy against online GBV, developed emergency responses during the war, and continued advancing regional feminist movement-building and SRHR awareness. The Strategic Partner focused on developing SRHR-related content and delivering trainings to different groups. The Oxfam Regonal Platform continued its partnership with their both women and youth led partner and engaged 1 new both women and youth led CSOs in 2024. The partnership will continue in 2025.

On regional and global level, consortium members strive for equal partnership. In 2025, the partnership entails SMEX, FEMALE, the Strategic Partner, the Oxfam MENA Regional Platform, RNW Media and Oxfam Novib. Among these SMEX, FEMALE and the Strategic Partner are "both women and youth led" organisations. Partners continued to collaborate in 2025 via ongoing co-creation, mutual capacity building and joint learning/expertise exchange.The Oxfam Regional Platform continued its partnership with a both women and youth led regional parter until July 2025, and its partnership with another both women and youth led regional partner until October 2025. The first partner's role was to raise awareness about SRHR by producing free courses. It also provided free and confidential onine SRHR counseling services to young women in the MENA region. The second partner's role was to build the capacity of youth in the area of SRHR advocacy, produce evidence-based advocacy materials, and facilitate youth access to international and regional advocacy spaces.In 2025, the escalation of the war had a direct and severe impact on civil society programming. Within the Strategic Partner's Masarouna program, the Advocacy Lab training cycle was brought to an abrupt end. The conflict notonly disrupted operational environments but also forced the discontinuation of all activities related to the facilitation of training sessions and broader capacity-building efforts with Advocacy Lab partners in the MENA region. As a result, the program’smomentum was interrupted, partners were unable to fully benefit from the learning trajectory, and planned knowledge transfer processes were put on hold indefinitely.

On regional and global level, consortium members strive for equal partnership. In decision making structure, consortium partners strive for co-creation and inclusive decision making. Consortium partners acknowledge that decision making processes can therefore take longer but it is imperative to ensure meaningful involvement of all partners. Oxfam Novib has supported AFE in their organisational development and governance restructuring to become a more stable and transparent organisation.

On regional and global level, consortium members strive for equal partnership. RNW Media is closely working together with all these partners on different levels through several working groups. The partnership between Oxfam Novib and Fe-Male led to a strengthened focus on feminist principles, and joint influencing activities around that subject. The partnership with the regional strategic partner gave increased insights in the challenges marginalized people face, and partnering with SMEX led to the start of increased focus on digital rights. All three partnerships will still need to further develop in the coming year, with more joint strategizing and joint activities to come. Oxfam Regional Platform has built a formal partnership with a both women and youth led organisation, which has trained young activists and shared SRHR information, as well as organised several regional events that aimed at facilitating access to key global spaces such as the CSW.Through the Digital Security Assesment activity, SMEX supported Fe-Male, the regional strategic partner and a local partner of Oxfam in country.

The partnership will be strengthened as the consortium partners get to know each other and each other's strengths better, which will enable a further increase in Southern leadership and strengthening of feminist ways of working. We would see the partnership evolve through collaboration, joint learning meetings, regular exchanges and possible introduction of new partners, which can be identified through the implementation and assessment of project activities

The partnership evolves through co-creation and mutual capacity building opportunities such as learning events and expertise exchange.The inclusion of SMEX, Fe-Male and the regional strategic partner in Masarouna means a renewed focus on Southern Leadership and increases the participation of youth and marginalized groups in the programme. SMEX will support Fe-Male in a digital assesment and Fe-Male will refer cases concerning marginalized groups for the regional strategic partner and ask for support for any related matter.
Oxfam Novib's partnership with Fe-Male strengthens the feminist principles of Masarouna and Oxfam's Novib partnership with the regional strategic partner enables joint advocacy for the rights of marginalized groups, and increases the focus of Masarouna activities on inclusion of marginalized populations. Oxfam Novib's partnership with SMEX will be centered around increasing digital safety and security for all partners in the project and advocating for digital rights as an essential element to access reliable SRHR information.
In 2023, a partner organisation of the Oxfam Regional Platform will provide opportunity for young people to advocate for their SRHR through participation at the Women Deliver conference, provide safe spacethrough closed feminist circles, covening with decision makers.

Masarouna’s strategic partner will give FEMALE a training on the rights and inclusion of marginalized groups, targeting all the staff in FEMALE. SMEX and FEMALE will collaborate in Bread & Net and we will continue to work on the assessment of digital security in collaboration with SMEX. FEMALE will support SMEX in their digital campaigns. The partnerships between RNW Media and SMEX, FEMALE and the strategic partner evolve through continuous co-creation, mutual capacity building and learning opportunities such as learning events and expertise exchange through CoP and working groups. comment.narrative: International instruments such as UPRs (Universal Period Reviews), VNRs (Voluntary National Reviews/SDGs) and CEDAW reports are a key tool for accountability for the SDGs and Human Rights treaties, including on SRHR and Civic Space, both at the national and global level. They provide an important opportunity for CSOs to hold their governments and global leaders accountable, especially for members of civil society who have limited space to participate in accountability processes at a national level.

Oxfam Regional Platform and its partners organised key events for youth activists, partner organizations and Oxfam staff to convene, reflect and exchange learning with others on topics, challenges and needs related to SRHR. Some events are expected to ultimately lead to creating more spaces for expressing the demands and positions of young people in terms of SRHR. A virtual training session was organised to demystify the ECOSOC accreditation application to the UN’s Committee on NGOs and the selection processes. It addressed common challenges that applicants face and how to overcome them. During the "Mujawara" activity, young visual artists from Masarouna countries gathered in one safe space to interact and talk about topics that are considered taboos in their countries.
The Human Rights Network (BMO), a network of 21 Dutch human rights and development organisations, of which Oxfam Novib is part, provided input to the Dutch Human Rights Ambassador ahead of her visit to the COP27. BMO members asked support for more civic space for CSOs, so that they could be present at the COP27 and freely express opinions in the press. An information sheet (prepared by Oxfam Novib with input from other BMO members) on the civic space situation was shared. No measureable civic space achievement could be observed, but there was a lot of media attention internationally around the issue of limited civic space for CSOs during the COP27.
Early 2023, Oxfam informed the Dutch Human Rights Ambassador about issues around SRHR, the position of activists and civil society, shrinking civic space, etc. in preparation of her visit to the MENA region in February. We also participated in the briefing meeting by the Human Rights Ambassador about her visit. In the meeting, better access to the Civic Space Fund & Flexfund was lobbied for. Oxfam advised about possible organisations/funds to support diverse young people to seek emergency support. (#1)
Qualitative information on the case concerned is the final report.

Update Oct. 2023: The Regional Policy Dialogue Meeting and the Enough Campaign (which has a dual objective: channeling voices and creating space for civic engagement) contribute to putting the concerns and needs of young people at the forefront of national and international conversations about SRHR. One Oxfam MENA Regional Platform partner will organize a panel discussion at CSW '24, advocating for the importance of gender-responsive financial solutions, a topic crucial for institutional development and resource allocation in SRH service provision. This partner will also create Virtual Empower Path empowering YP in the MENA region in the area of SRHR through addressing the immediate gaps in SRHR knowledge and services and strengthening youth engagementin civil society at (inter)national levels. Oxfam Novib offered its support to Oxfam country teams and (consortium) partners for engaging in Universal Periodic Reviews (UPRs), Voluntary National Reviews (VNRs) and CEDAW processes, to use these processesto create space for their demands on SRHR for young people. However the demand for such support has been limited, because Oxfam country offices and partners were either already engaged in these processes, or were not yet planning to work on this. Oxfam Novib, in coordination with consortium partners, will rather support country teams and partners in (inter)national (for instance Dutch/European) platforms and policy dialogues and support alliance building of national level CSOs to advocate and create space for their demands and positions on SRHR for young people. Because of the shrinking civic space in all Masarouna countries, Oxfam Novib is bringing down its 5-year target from 8 to 3. Based on low realization at midterm, the Oxfam MENA RP is lowering itfrom 5 to 3. The consolidated target has hence been adjusted from 8 to 6 cases at midterm, where we have added together the targets of the Oxfam RP (#3) and Oxfam Novib (#3), as they operate at different levels

To this end, Oxfam Novib invested in designing a Youth Peer Learning Trajectory during the final quarter of 2022, that aims to bring young people together from all six countries and the regional level in a peer exchange and strategy development. The Youth Peer Learning Trajectory will be implemented during the first half of 2023. RNW Media will further help Masarouna to develop a digital environment that fosters learning in this learning trajectory. Two individuals from RNW Media partners will be following the youth learning trajectory who can also apply to become part of Masarouna youth advisory board in 2023.

As a result of close collaboration and co-creation sessions, Oxfam Novib and RNW Media have defined a regional youth engagement strategy by the end of 2022 and will have a position on how youth' representation can be enhanced and monitored in our programmes. The youth engagement strategy will consist of offline and online engagement components, with the participation of countries/national youth advisory committees and/or the main youth actors identified through the youth mapping exercise. The strategy will include a division of roles and responsibilities of youth participants in the rolling out of the strategy including youth identified indicators on how participants identify both their role and the change they want to achieve.

Oxfam Novib and Masarouna country teams will further develop our meaningful youth engagement approach and processes over the course of 2023. This includes working with young activists from the targeted countries in enhancing and implementing their own influencing activities and towards better representation of young people in the work of national and regional organisations and the provision of technical support by Oxfam Novib on developing youth-centered approaches.

comment.narrative:
Young people and marginalized groups face challenges with regard to meaningful participation in international political processes and events, such as HLPF and CSW. Data on specific digital communities providing and accessing online SRHR information is often collected on country level but a regional merge of information (that can be used for regional advocacy) is lacking. Regional partners are connected to different extents on a regional level with groups and activists. They have the ability to expand the networks but so far they lacked the resources online and offline to expand this network. One of the regional partners seeks to support young people with innovative means to advocate for their SRHR.. Oxfam Regional Platform through the Enough! campaign indirectly engages youth in generating initiatives on their SRHR as well as through supporting youth networks this will encourage generating initiatives/trainings in their respective countries.
There is currently a lack of social media policy analysis, which is needed to develop a advocacy campaign to enhance these social media platforms policies.

*For International Women’s Day, RNW Media and Masarouna partners conducted a digital advocacy campaign for safe, equal online spaces for women, using joint brainstorming and content creation tools. The campaign reached over 25,000 people, with strong engagement and contributions to challenging social norms.*Three regional advocacy initiatives by civil society partners in the Advocacy Lab focused on strengthening youth-led SRHR advocacy in restrictive environments, with participants developing context-specific approaches.*SMEX and HRW launched a campaign on digital targeting and safety in the MENA region, urging META to take action based on research findings, resulting in recognition and online advocacy*Five regional advocacy initiatives were implemented through the MENA Regional Platform and partners to advance inclusive SRHR policies and challenge harmful norms for YP in the MENA region, with YP as key actors.*RNW Media coordinated a digital advocacy initiative for International Women’s Day to promote safer digital spaces for women and girls. The campaign was co-created with a regional partner and included a digital event, shaped by diverse partner input.*Six regional advocacy initiatives through the MENA Regional Platform and partners advanced SRHR andyouth advocacy. Activities included supporting youth at CSW69, developing policy briefs on menopause and crisis-related GBV, producing a theatre piece on SRHR realities, and engaging decision-makers in Brussels, EEAS, and INTPA. The MENA Regional Platform supported youth-led SRHR research and participation in SRHR webinars.*Qualitative information on 17 other advocacy initiatives are included in the final report.

SMEX invited 21 partners from the 6 Masarouna countries for the upcoming 3-days Bread&Net 2023 event. 4 partners submitted a proposal for sessions about SRHR. It is envisioned that this will lead to collective advocacy initiatives in the future.
In 2023, the Advocacy Lab was held by Masarouna's Strategic Partner, gathering 4 CSOs operating in the Masarouna geographic scope. The CSOs were trained on Community Organizing, Tactical Mapping and Adaptive leadership, MEAL and proposal writing. Following the12-days training, the CSOs were invited to develop an advocacy campaign each, write a proposal and submit it to the Strategic Partner by the end of September 2023.
One of the regional partners of the Oxfam MENA regional platform co-organized with the capital-based Film Society the SRHR Film Days in 2022. 19 short films from various countries were screened, each screening followed by a panel discussion, engaging young people with artists, filmmakers, civil society grassroots and seasoned activists, in hopes of creating strong and innovative alliances and networks (#1) The regional partner was involved for the first time in the annual session of the Commission on the Status of Women (CSW). The director of the same partner was co-chair of the CSW NGO Arab Caucus Convening, which organised eight events on various topics, including SRHR. These events created spaces for meaningful dialogue and knowledge-sharing among activists, feminist funds, international donors, and UN staff. (#2)
In 2023, Oxfam Novib hosted an all-youth virtual panel event and side event during the Women Deliver 2023 Conference. Through these events, 8 young leaders from Masarouna made their voices heard at this critical space for SRHR advocacy.(#3)
A Youth Advocacy Task Force was set up, consisting of a group of youth activists from each Masarouna country, who shall connect national and international influencing in a youth-led way and steer and take lead in international influencing.

Update Oct. 2023: The MENA Regional Platform (RP) will support various regional advocacy initiatives. E.g. the "Is Enough" campaign, engaging young advocates in the campaign's implementation. The RP will also organize a Regional Policy Dialogue Meeting on the intersection between climate change and SRHR, underscoring their support for youth engagement. One RP partner will organise a side event on gender responsive financial solutions at CSW ‘24. In addition, we aim to spark policy discussions at the national level based on the outcomes of the regional youth conference. RNW Media will co-create global advocacy campaigns with/by/for YP related to SRHR that are mostly linked with international days (e.g. 16 days of activism). These will be based on RNW Media's campaign calendar that will be rolled out late 2023. RNW Media will e.g. use country specific cases from Masarouna to develop a campaign to prevent censorship on social media. Oxfam Novib will facilitate a youth-led coalition at CSW ‘24, supportingthem to develop their agenda and strategy during this event. ONL will also support the organisation of a conference in Amman during which young participants will discuss obstacles in obtaining SRHR education and information, develop policy recommendations, and together with CSOs share these with invited key policymakers. SMEX will invite young people to the annual Bread&Net conference to discuss lessons learned, challenges and opportunities around digital rights and the intersection of the Internet and SRHR. Based on the policy analysis research and SMEX's help desk cases related to SRHR, SMEX will lead an advocacy campaign targeting these companies policies. At midterm the original 5-year target proved to be too ambitious. The consolidated target has therefore been adjusted from 20 to 10 advocacy initiatives at all other levels, where we have added together the highest target at global level (RNW Media #4) and the highest target at regional level (Oxfam MENA RP #6).

comment.narrative: The Dutch government has a leadership role on SRHR funding in the world. However, the current Grant Instrument SRHR Partnership Fund, Policy Framework for Strengthening Civil Society of the Dutch government is ending in 2025. Southern based CSOs, in particular WROs, depend on access to this type of funding to do their work.

In close collaboration with other Dutch civil society organisations and with partners from the South, Oxfam Novib advocated for the following elements to be included in the Feminist foreign policy developed by the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA): ensuring more inclusiveness in terms of programmes supported and of language used, ensuring easier access to funding; putting a greater emphasis on gender equality. The Feminist foreign policy is expected o be implemented from mid-2023.
The Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) has agreed to implement the policy (letter has been shared with Parliament) and MoFA is finalising its Feminist foreign policy handbook, which operationalises the policy and will most likely be launched in September/October 2023. Oxfam Novib contributed in the numerous review rounds and specifically payed attention to intersectionality in the policy, continued meaningful consultation of marginalised groups as well as access to funding for organisations (including youth andfeminist) in the Global South vis à vis reporting requirements
Qualitative information on the 3 governmental policies concerned is included in the final report.

Update Oct. 2023: Oxfam Novib aims at having 2 governmental policies adopted in The Netherlands, in close collaboration with other Dutch civil society organisations and with partners from the South: - Launch of a Feminist Foreign Policy (FFP), reflecting the commitment of the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA) to keep (and preferably expand) their leadership role in the world on SRHR and for funding to stay available (specifically for Southern based WROs organizations) to promote and work on gender equality and social inclusion within their own contexts. - (New target): A policy decision to ensure the overall budget allocated to development cooperation (which is currently under pressure) increases, or at least remains the same, including an increased funding for SRHR programming. This is done through various influencing activities, such as monitoring the election process by reviewing and providing input for party programmes, launching the Sekswijzer (an election tool on SRHR), organising (together with the SRHR platform) an SRHR election debate, lobbying for SRHR and gender to be mainstreamed in the Afrika strategy and SRHR to be a key part of the global health strategy. The quantitative 5-year target for this indicator was adjusted from 1 to 2 governernment policies at midterm.
